evidence: In Fig. 1 we report the XRR patterns recorded from the Co(8.1 nm)/Sb2Te3 and Co(6.3 nm)/Pt stacks obtained after 250 ALD cycles of Co deposition. The two structures were modelled with a multilayer stack and, from the best fit of the data, we extracted the thickness, roughness, and electronic density (ρ) values for each layer (Table 1). In particular, for the Co/Sb2Te3 sample, the value of the electronic density is slightly lower than nominal values for bulk Co (2.37–2.44 e−/Å3), as typically observed in thin films. The stacking of the Co/Pt sample was modelled introducing an interlayer between Co and Pt (see the Electronic Supplementary Material (ESM)). The electronic density of this layer is within the 3.3 –4.9 e−/Å3 range, which corresponds to the values of crystalline PtO and Pt, respectively. XRR measurements conducted on the bare Pt substrate prior to Co deposition evidenced a surface roughness of 1.2 ± 0.1 nm, which is a quite high value for heavy metals deposited by conventional magnetron sputtering (see the ESM). These results, jointly with the relatively high roughness of the interlayer (1 ± 0.1 nm), suggest the presence of a partial oxidation of the Pt surface, likely organized in PtOx islands, which could not be removed with the 180 °C mild annealing during the Co deposition. Interestingly, to describe the XRR data collected for the Co/Sb2Te3 sample, no interlayer was introduced in the fitting model. Although an intermixed region between Co and Sb2Te3 could exist, it turned out to be much thinner than in the Fe/Sb2Te3 system, and well beyond the XRR detection limit. The structural integrity and the layer thickness of the thickest samples (1,000 cycles) was checked by the scanning electron microscope (SEM) cross sections shown in the inset of Fig. 1. In order to get a further insight about the morphology of our materials, we performed atomic force microscopy (AFM) both at the surface of Sb2Te3 prior to the ALD of Co, and on top of the final Co(8.1 nm)/Sb2Te3 heterostructure. From the AFM analysis on a 2 μm × 2 μm area, the granular nature of the Sb2Te3 thin film and its structural continuity were confirmed (Fig. 2(a)). Moreover, the root-meansquare (RMS) roughness turned out to be 2.2 ± 0.1 nm, in very good accordance with the 2.3 ± 0.1 nm value extracted from the XRR model and reported in Table 1. In Fig. 2(b) the AFM for the Co(8.1 nm)/Sb2Te3 heterostructure is reported. Herein, the uniformity of the Co thin film was confirmed, and the RMS roughness was found to be 2.8 ± 0.1 nm, being quite lower than the value extracted by XRR. The XRR technique is sensitive to both the morphological roughness and the density grading between two layers, thus typically giving higher roughness than AFM, also supporting the presence of an oxidized layer at the Co surface.
